item.title: You Can Now Order McDonald’s Through Discord
item.description: Discord has launched a McDonald's app, allowing users to order food through one of the most popular communication platforms.
item.content:encoded:
Discord has launched a McDonald's app, allowing users to order food through one of the most popular communication platforms.

The integration, powered by Uber Eats, comes with its own lofi-inspired interface unique to Discord. The new app arrives just as gamers are starting to get their hands on GTA 6, the biggest game launch of all time, and it seems McDonald’s was worried players wouldn’t even be willing to look down at their phone screen.

The 'Order McDonald’s' feature is found in the Apps section of any Discord DM, channel, or server. You can choose to launch the app in a given server, which notifies everyone that you’re ordering McDonald’s, or access the app privately through its own DM.

Once inside, you get the option to Order Food or Play Game. Yes, there’s a game, but first, let’s talk about the food. Discord claims the purpose of the integration is to let you order food without tabbing out of a game or call. Yet, hitting the Order Food option actually takes you to an external Uber Eats link.

If you have the Uber Eats app, Discord on mobile takes you straight to your account, while the desktop version opens your default browser. In either case, you’ll need an Uber Eats account to actually order anything, and you’ll definitely still have to hit pause on whatever you're playing. At the very least, hitting the Order Food option gives you a neat little animation to approach the Drive-Thru window.

Now we can talk about the game. Fast Lane Feast is for when "you’re waiting for your order to arrive," but you can play the new minigame at any time. You drive along a little street, collecting burgers and fries for fuel, flying off ramps, and trying to avoid traffic. Controls are pretty minimal - using A and D to move left and right - but if you do get competitive, you can save your score to a global leaderboard.

McDonald’s isn’t the only fast-food chain testing trying to attract some loyal gamers. Wendy’s just launched an entire RPG, one of the very few game releases in the month of GTA 6. Wendy’s has also teased a collab with the Rockstar game, and McDonald’s might be the only company on the planet that hasn’t. For now, McDonald’s is offering the Pokémon Happy Meal, with a Home Alone collaboration planned for the holiday season.
item.dc:creator: Blythe Dujardin

item.title: Rockstar President Sam Houser Issues Rare Statement to Celebrate GTA 6 Launch
item.description: As GTA 6 launches around the world, Rockstar president and co-founder Sam Houser has issued a rare statement to celebrate the occasion and "many more years" of experiences ahead.
item.content:encoded:
As GTA 6 launches around the world, Rockstar president and co-founder Sam Houser has issued a rare statement to celebrate the occasion and "many more years" of experiences ahead.

While other high-ranking Rockstar staff have discussed GTA 6 in interviews thus far, the famously reclusive producer has now outlined his company's intentions with the game, and suggested there was much more to come in future.

"Rockstar Games was founded on the belief that games could achieve the same distinction as all other forms of storytelling, become essential to modern culture, and to be thought of as stories and worlds that live on with all of us," Houser began, in a statement shared with IGN's GTA 6 reviewer, Luke Reilly.

"This week, Grand Theft Auto returns to Leonida and modern-day Vice City. While things have changed and time has passed, one aspect holds true: We have tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of, and why we believe games are so special.

"Whether you can trace your journey to this game through the entire series or are experiencing Grand Theft Auto for the first time, this is a narrative set in a world full of possibilities — and it is up to you as the player to shape how it ultimately feels, and concludes.

"We hope it felt both familiar and entirely new, and above all, we hope that you had fun. We are incredibly grateful to you and everything that you do to celebrate games. We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with you.

"Thank you, Sam Houser."

While Houser's rare statement is notable enough on its own, the mention of "many more years" of experiences from Rockstar will inevitably excite fans already wondering what's next from the company. While the base GTA 6 offers hundreds of hours of experiences to discover and enjoy, there is of course huge speculation surrounding the game's unannounced but inevitable online portion. As of yet, Rockstar has not discussed its next iteration of GTA Online at all, though fans expect to hear something of it sooner or later.

The current GTA 5 version of GTA Online has raked in around $5 billion so far since its arrival back in 2013. Another version seems less a matter of if rather than when, though exactly how it will differ, and what will become of the existing service all remains under wraps.

IGN has everything you need for the launch of GTA 6, including the GTA 6 global release times, as well as details on the last-minute PS5 update you'll need to download. In case you missed it, last night we learned the real-life identity of GTA 6's Lucia. And we're now live with our GTA 6 launch blog, which we'll use to fill you in on everything else about the game over the coming hours.
item.dc:creator: Tom Phillips

item.title: Saros Is Over 50% Off at Walmart Ahead of Black Friday, but YMMV on Spotting the Deal
item.description: Walmart has slashed just over $40 off a physical copy of Saros on PS5 ahead of its Black Friday sale, bringing it down to $29.97 from its original MSRP of $69.99. YMMV on being able to score this deal, though.
item.content:encoded:
Physical PS5 copies of Saros may have hit $40 as part of PlayStation's Black Friday sale, but Walmart's offering them for even cheaper right now ahead of its Black Friday sale. The game is currently marked down to $29.97 at the retailer, which is a massive discount of $40.02 off its original MSRP of $69.99, but YMMV on being able to spot this deal.

While my editor was able to see this price right away, I initially ran into a problem trying to find it. If you encountered the same issue as me of seeing $41.99 instead as a deal price, don't worry. Just scroll down to the 'Other sellers' section and you should see this $29.97 offer, which is sold and shipped by Walmart, available to add to your cart.

It may be a bit of a hoop to jump through to get there (if you run into the price problem, that is), but this is one fantastic offer to jump on while it's available. It's the lowest price it's ever hit at Walmart, according to our research, and as far as PS5 game deals go, it's certainly a highlight among the selection of physical games on sale right now.

In general, if Housemarque's latest has been on your gaming wishlist, this is a perfect opportunity to pick it up for your PS5 library. IGN's Michael Higham called it "a test of skill that's as much a rhythmic dance as it is a fireworks show with a punch-packing sci-fi arsenal" in his review, and highlights that "while it's eclipsed by its predecessor in some important ways, Saros was still worth banging my head against over and over again."

If you're curious what other PS5 games are discounted right now, PlayStation's Black Friday sale is in full swing and is chock-full of physical game deals. From Ghost of Yotei to Marvel's Wolverine to Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls, there's plenty to look through right now. We'll be keeping an eye out for even more game deals that may drop as other retailer's start up their Black Friday sales soon, too.

item.title: In GTA 6, Doomscrolling Is a Necessity If You Want to See Everything
item.description: Scrolling social media in GTA 6 is more than a distraction - it can help you see everything the world has to offer.
item.content:encoded:
Ever since that first trailer, we knew social media would play an important part in GTA 6. A good chunk of those first 90 seconds was faux TikTok footage, after all. And now that reviews are out, and the game is live in New Zealand, Australia, and many other places on that side of the planet, we have a better idea of how GTA 6’s in-universe social media operates. One thing’s for certain: you’ll need to be scrolling if you want to see everything the world has to offer.

As part of IGN’s Ask Me Anything livestream earlier today, reviewer Luke Reilly explained how he unlocked a new mission chain based on a post he saw on Snapmatic, the GTA universe’s parody of Instagram.

“I was scrolling through the game’s social media, and I saw a post from this guy on a farm looking for a pilot, and it pings it on the map for you,” he said. “It’ll ping in an undiscovered part of the map that there’s something there because you’ve spotted it on social media.”

IGN’s Simon Cardy, who has also played over 100 hours of the game and is currently answering your questions over on our launch live blog, confirms that he also used social media to discover new opportunities, which are then automatically pinned to the game’s map.

Simon also notes that you’ll hear about opportunities on the in-game radio, although those are hints you’ll need to follow up on yourself – only certain mediums will pin a mission to your map. Aside from social media posts, pamphlets on local bulletin boards will also drop mission markers on your map, something Luke described in today’s AMA: “One of the cool things is that you see signs around [advertising] for a pilot. It’s visual storytelling; you can [follow the instructions] and go there and do jobs for this character that you meet.”

Bulletin boards are, of course, nothing new for video games – you’ll no doubt have picked up hundreds of bounties and side quests from boards in dozens of RPGs across the years. But GTA 6’s use of the internet and social media is more novel. Simon also notes that there are connections to be found across the in-game web, too – a story on the news app may lead you to investigate a topic on Snapmatic, which in turn will pin a new mission to the map.

In short: we may call it doomscrolling in real life, but it’s a pretty handy activity to do in GTA 6. While I expect there will be multiple ways to stumble across the game’s many, many missions, it seems a fun and authentic method to discover things on social media.

For more GTA 6, be sure to check out our breakdown of how long it takes to complete its campaign, as well as our brand new interview with Rockstar’s Rob Nelson. And if you want to see the game in action, you can watch 15 minutes of the game’s first mission.

GTA 6 on IGN - The Biggest Stories at Launch

Grand Theft Auto 6 has launched in the most easterly regions of the world, and with it comes many exciting new details about the most-hyped video game ever developed. You’re in the right place to learn everything you need to know about Rockstar’s latest.

  • We awarded GTA 6 a 10 in our review, with writer Luke Reilly stating that it is “the single most impressive video game I have ever played.”
  • Perhaps unsurprisingly with a response like that, GTA 6 is now the joint-highest rated game of all time.
  • Our new interview with head of development Rob Nelson reveals how GTA 6 came together at Rockstar North.
  • Curious how long GTA 6 is? Our comparison of four different playthroughs from four different writers reveals it can extend way past the runtimes of previous Rockstar games.
  • Playing on Xbox? We’ve tested performance on Xbox Series S, as well as showcased gameplay from Xbox Series X.
  • If you’ve picked up the more expensive version of GTA 6, here’s how the Ultimate Edition content works.
item.dc:creator: Matt Purslow

item.title: Last Chance to Save $10 Off GTA 6 Ultimate Edition on PS5 and Xbox Ahead of Launch
item.content:encoded:
Hard to believe, but we’re mere hours away from the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. I for one am pumped to play it, especially after we gave it a 10/10 in our review. If you still haven’t locked in a preorder for GTA 6, I have some excellent news for you: whether you’re planning to play on PS5 or Xbox Series X|S, you can save $10 today, using the steps below. But do it soon, because these gift card discounts tend to sell out within just a few hours of going live.

All you have to do is buy a digital gift card at Newegg, enter a promo code at checkout, and you’ll get $100 worth of digital currency for $90. And as luck would have it, the Ultimate edition of GTA 6 costs $100. So if you turn around and preorder the game, you’re saving $10 instantly. If you haven’t preordered yet, this is the best deal you’ll find to play GTA 6 at launch.

Step 1: Buy a Discounted Gift Card at Newegg

  • PS5: Click here and enter promo code BNWF3453 at checkout
  • Xbox: Click here and enter promo code BNWF3451 at checkout

It's easy to forget to enter the promo code, so make sure you do so before finalizing your purchase or you won't save $10. Within an hour after you place your order, you'll receive an email with a redeemable code for your digital gift card (I bought a PlayStation gift card and it arrived 6 minutes later).

Step 2: Redeem the Gift Card

  • PS5: Sign in and click here to redeem your gift card
  • Xbox: Sign in and click here to redeem your gift card

Use the links above and sign into your account. Then click your avatar in the upper right of the page and select "Redeem Code" from the dropdown menu. Paste the code in there, and now you should now have $100 in your digital wallet.

Step 3: Buy GTA 6

  • PS5: Standard Edition ($79.99) | Ultimate Edition ($99.99)
  • Xbox: Standard Edition ($79.99) | Ultimate Edition ($99.99)

The final step is buying the game. You have two options: the standard edition or the ultimate edition for $20 more.

The standard edition gets you the game, along with the Vintage Vice City Pack as a preorder bonus (see below), and one month of GTA+. The Ultimate edition includes all of that, plus “an exclusive collection of premium vehicles, weapons, apparel, and action threaded across all aspects of Jason and Lucia’s story.” Here's a lengthy breakdown of what's included.

GTA 6 Ultimate Edition Contents

Purchasing the ultimate edition will get you the following items:

Exclusive Vehicles & Storage

  • Vapid Dominator Buggy with access to the Paradise Garage, including a weapon locker and stash box.
  • '95 Grotti Cheetah sports car with a retro-inspired design.
  • Dinka Enduro motorcycle, Crest Kayak, and exclusive Vapid Ganado pickup truck upgrades at Jason's Safehouse.
  • Shitzu Squalo speedboat equipped with a weapons crate.

Extra Vehicle Content

  • Access to two exclusive vehicle customization shops:
    • Rideout Customs (Vice City)
    • One-Eyed Willie's (Lake Leonida)
  • Classic Car Collection side activity featuring restoration projects, including four Ultimate Edition-exclusive vehicles.

Exclusive Weapons

  • Hawk & Little Morgan Revolver with unique Vice City-themed designs for Jason and Lucia.
  • Personalized versions of Jason's Girardi ES9 pistol and Lucia's Klose K17 pistol.

Additional Missions & Activities

  • PTT Youngin$ Compound content, including a special robbery opportunity and exclusive contraband rewards.

Cosmetics & Character Customization

  • Exclusive outfits, tattoos, and accessories for Jason and Lucia.
  • Goodtime Gear clothing collection.
  • Access to Stock 305, an exclusive streetwear store.
  • Exclusive hairstyles, makeup, nails, and facial hair options from Sara's Unisex Salon.
  • Over 50 exclusive tattoos from Electric Fang Tattoo.

Preorder Bonus: GTA 6 Vintage Vice City Pack Contents

Preordering either version (standard or ultimate) will get you the following items:

  • ’55 Vapid Stanier and Shore Court Garage: Cruise Shore Drive in the legendary ’55 Vapid Stanier, a Vice City classic meant to be admired, and store it in a new personal garage just a stone’s throw from the glistening sands of Ocean Beach. Like all personal garages in Leonida, you’ll have a weapon locker to customize your loadout for any occasion plus a secure place to deposit stolen goods for the local Fence, who will accept most stolen goods at a reasonably discounted rate.
  • Outfits and Hairstyles: Dress for excess with two Vice City luxury looks for both Jason and Lucia:
    • Jason: An effortlessly chic linen suit in vintage pastel, complemented by the cut and coif of the decade of decadence.
    • Lucia: The world is yours in a red sequin mini dress and curls.
  • Exclusive Weapon Pattern: Channel the original Vice City kingpin, Tommy Vercetti, and his iconic palm tree button-up with a tropical pattern available to adorn most guns.

You can find more info in our GTA 6 preorder guide.

This deal has come and gone a few times since GTA 6 went up for preorder, and it has always been incredibly popular among our readers. Because of its popularity, the deal always sells out before the end of the day. So if you haven’t bought GTA 6 yet and you want to save $10, do this ASAP.

If you want more, you can get a very cool-looking GTA 6-themed PS5 DualSense controller, which launches alongside the game. Also, check out GTA 6: The Album, which is also up for preoder. That's not to be confused with GTA 6: The Original Score, which features music you'll hear in the game. Clearly, Rockstar is giving players plenty of ways to spend money on all things GTA 6.

And here's a fun tip for anyone who made it this far. Preodrering the game on Xbox will allow you to use the New Zealand time zone trick to play early (shh, don’t tell anyone I told you). Otherwise you can check out the global release times here.

item.title: MindsEye Dev Build a Rocket Boy Says Legal Action Against 'Several Third Parties' Will Help It Pay Off Its Mountain of Debt
item.description: After the disastrous release of MindsEye, its collapsed developer, Build a Rocket Boy (BARB), is attempting to pay off its mountain of debt via legal action against “saboteurs” who it alleged contributed to the game's downfall.
item.content:encoded:
After the disastrous release of MindsEye, its collapsed developer, Build a Rocket Boy (BARB), is attempting to pay off its mountain of debt via legal action against “saboteurs” who it alleged contributed to the game's downfall.

Story-driven action adventure game MindsEye was initially designed to be a part of Everywhere, the ‘Roblox for adults’ creation platform led by former Grand Theft Auto design chief Leslie Benzies. BARB eventually switched to focus on MindsEye, with the company ballooning in size to over 500 staff at peak.

But MindsEye flopped hard when it came out in June 2025, with players calling it "broken," "buggy," and "the worst game of 2025." Soon after, BARB said it was “heartbroken” over the issues players had faced with the game, and promised to release a series of patches to fix the significant performance problems, glitches, and AI behavior bugs. Amid sweeping layoffs, Benzies told staff that the studio would bounce back and relaunch MindsEye, blaming its struggles on internal and external "saboteurs," among other things. CEO Mark Gerhard said the studio had been investigating what he called “criminal activity” that took place around the launch of the game.

However, in September this year it was reported that the Edinburgh-based company faced closure, with BARB slipping into administration. Today, on the eve of GTA 6's launch, an administrators’ proposal went live on BARB’s Companies House page — spotted by RedbullCola on ResetEra, (thanks Kotaku). The proposal details what BARB owes and to who, as well as how it plans to cover its debts.

The total debt comes to £61.7 million (approx. $81.2 million). The bulk of the debt belongs to NetEase (£36.4 million, approx. $47.9 million). NetEase is a major investor in BARB, having participated in multiple funding rounds including a $110 million Series D round in January 2024. According to company documents, BARB brought in more than £233 million (approx. $306 million) of investment by 2024. £19.90 (approx. $25... yes, $25!) is owed to ChatGPT company OpenAI.

Earlier this year, BARB co-CEO Mark Gerhard claimed the studio was a victim of corporate espionage and "saboteurs." The company will now pursue litigation against the people it accused in a bid to gather the money and pay off the debts. Gerhard had pinned the blame on a YouTube and TikTok management agency called Ritual Network, accusing it of tarnishing BARB’s reputation in a coordinated propaganda campaign. Ritual Network has denied all allegations that it orchestrated a $1 million smear campaign against MindsEye.

The proposal claims BARB’s investigations against “a number of third parties” are “the largest asset of the administration,” so it seems like all hopes at the company of paying off the debt are tied to litigation being successful.

Here is BARB's claim from the company document filed today:

Prior to the Company's entry into Administration, the directors had been investigating the circumstances surrounding the commercial performance of the video game, MindsEye, which was released in 2025 following significant development investment. The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary.

The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties.

The directors have indicated that any such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions.

In May, Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, issued what sounded like a nod to BARB’s struggles. "Making hits seems to get harder and harder and harder as entertainment industries mature," Zelnick said, speaking at the TD Cowen 54th Annual Technology, Media & Telecom Conference.

"The folks at Rockstar seem to be able to make these massive hits, and lots of other people have tried. Lots and lots, including former Rockstar employees. And so far, they haven't been able to do it."
item.dc:creator: Kirk McKeand
